parameters.meaning: 0 = correctly calibrated .. 1 = fully drifted low: nuisance-trips below the breaker's true rated current (bimetal spring aging fatigue, or an SSPC's own reference/firmware drift)

parameters.name: contact_resistance
parameters.meaning: 0 = clean contacts .. 1 = welded/fused by repeated arcing: raises the I2t heat (and magnetic instantaneous multiple) the mechanism needs before it can still force the contacts open, up to effectively never

failures.cause: Differential pressure rises until the 35 psi bypass valve cracks (reaches the cockpit as the real `ENG n FUEL FILTER CLOGGED` FbwProc, deep/ecam/fbw/generated.rs); past 60 psi the bypass valve opens and reaches the cockpit as the real `ENG n FUEL SYS CONTAMINATION` FbwProc, deep/ecam/fbw/ata70.rs.

failures.cause: The bypass-warning monitor itself reads faulted independent of the element's real clog state (`ENG n FUEL FILTER MONITORING FAULT`, FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM p.5784: "The fuel filter is no longer monitored").

failures.cause: Internal slip flow grows as 1/(1-wear)^2; delivered flow falls short of the theoretical displacement flow, starving the FMU and reaching the cockpit through the real `ENG n THRUST LOSS` FbwProc (deep/ecam/fbw/ata70.rs) once the shortfall is severe enough to matter.
failures.name: Engine 1 HP fuel pump wear

failures.cause: Caps delivered flow directly, regardless of slip -- there is simply not enough fuel arriving to fill the gear pockets; same real `ENG n THRUST LOSS` path as the wear fault above.
failures.name: Engine 1 HP fuel pump inlet starvation

failures.cause: Actuator slew rate falls to zero; the valve tracks the commanded flow ever more slowly and, fully stuck, freezes in place; a large enough error reaches the cockpit through the real `ENG n THRUST LOSS` FbwProc (deep/ecam/fbw/ata70.rs, on A32NX_ENG_n_THRUST_ABNORMAL/A32NX_ENG_n_FMU_FAULT).
failures.name: Engine 1 FMU metering valve sticking

failures.cause: The regulated differential collapses toward zero; metered flow starves even at full valve area (flameout risk); same real `ENG n THRUST LOSS` path as the metering valve fault above.
failures.name: Engine 1 FMU spill valve stuck open

failures.cause: The differential rises toward the raw HP pump discharge pressure; over-meters flow for a given commanded area; same real `ENG n THRUST LOSS` path as the metering valve fault above.
failures.name: Engine 1 FMU spill valve stuck closed

failures.cause: Travel rate scaled to zero; stuck open defeats a fire-handle shutdown, stuck closed flames the engine out and blocks a restart; reaches the cockpit through the real `ENG n HP FUEL VLV FAULT` FbwProc (deep/ecam/fbw/ata70.rs, FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM p.5789).

failures.cause: Differential pressure rises until the 12 psi bypass valve cracks (FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM p.5787); beyond that, undelivered debris passes on to the fine filter downstream.
failures.name: Engine 4 fuel strainer clog

failures.cause: Differential pressure rises until the 35 psi bypass valve cracks (reaches the cockpit as the real `ENG n FUEL FILTER CLOGGED` FbwProc, deep/ecam/fbw/generated.rs); past 60 psi the bypass valve opens and reaches the cockpit as the real `ENG n FUEL SYS CONTAMINATION` FbwProc, deep/ecam/fbw/ata70.rs.
failures.name: Engine 4 fuel filter clog

failures.cause: The bypass-warning monitor itself reads faulted independent of the element's real clog state (`ENG n FUEL FILTER MONITORING FAULT`, FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM p.5784: "The fuel filter is no longer monitored").
failures.name: Engine 4 fuel filter monitor fault

failures.cause: Internal slip flow grows as 1/(1-wear)^2; delivered flow falls short of the theoretical displacement flow, starving the FMU and reaching the cockpit through the real `ENG n THRUST LOSS` FbwProc (deep/ecam/fbw/ata70.rs) once the shortfall is severe enough to matter.
failures.name: Engine 4 HP fuel pump wear

failures.cause: Caps delivered flow directly, regardless of slip -- there is simply not enough fuel arriving to fill the gear pockets; same real `ENG n THRUST LOSS` path as the wear fault above.
failures.name: Engine 4 HP fuel pump inlet starvation

failures.cause: Actuator slew rate falls to zero; the valve tracks the commanded flow ever more slowly and, fully stuck, freezes in place; a large enough error reaches the cockpit through the real `ENG n THRUST LOSS` FbwProc (deep/ecam/fbw/ata70.rs, on A32NX_ENG_n_THRUST_ABNORMAL/A32NX_ENG_n_FMU_FAULT).
failures.name: Engine 4 FMU metering valve sticking

failures.cause: The regulated differential collapses toward zero; metered flow starves even at full valve area (flameout risk); same real `ENG n THRUST LOSS` path as the metering valve fault above.
failures.name: Engine 4 FMU spill valve stuck open

failures.cause: The differential rises toward the raw HP pump discharge pressure; over-meters flow for a given commanded area; same real `ENG n THRUST LOSS` path as the metering valve fault above.
failures.name: Engine 4 FMU spill valve stuck closed

failures.cause: Travel rate scaled to zero; stuck open defeats a fire-handle shutdown, stuck closed flames the engine out and blocks a restart; reaches the cockpit through the real `ENG n HP FUEL VLV FAULT` FbwProc (deep/ecam/fbw/ata70.rs, FCOM PRO-ABN-ECAM p.5789).

failures.cause: An orifice in the pressurised gallery: flow out goes as the square root of gallery pressure, so quantity falls fastest at high power and stops once the engine is shut down. Pressure itself barely moves until the falling level uncovers the pump's inlet, then follows the quantity down (physics::engine::oil::OilSystem) -- published as A32NX_ENG_n_GASPATH_OIL_QUANTITY_FRAC/_GASPATH_OIL_PRESS_PSI; no FCOM alert exists for a low-quantity reading by itself, but a severe enough leak starves pressure past 25 psi and reaches the cockpit through the real `ENG n OIL PRESS LO` FbwProc (deep/ecam/fbw/ata70.rs).

failures.cause: Same Euler blade work but less becomes useful pressure rise: compressor exit pressure falls for the same speed, and EGT rises for the same fuel flow/speed as the governor works to hold N under load.
failures.name: APU core compressor erosion

failures.cause: Less shaft work extracted per unit expansion: more of the gas's enthalpy survives to the exit (higher EGT) and the governor must burn more fuel to hold governed N under the same load.
failures.name: APU turbine damage

failures.cause: Lower delivered bleed pressure for the same demand and spool speed.
failures.name: APU load/bleed compressor erosion

failures.cause: Vanes freeze at their current opening; if that is closed relative to current demand, bleed delivery is starved even though the aircraft calls for more.
failures.name: APU load compressor IGV actuator jam

failures.cause: Cannot open to recirculate flow when bleed demand drops faster than it can follow: the load compressor's operating point falls below its surge line and it genuinely surges (compressor_map.rs::Point.in_surge).
failures.name: APU surge control valve actuator jam

failures.cause: More current for less torque at the same speed: a slower, weaker start, and in severe cases the core never reaches light-off speed.
failures.name: APU starter motor degradation/failure

failures.cause: At full failure the threshold sits at/above self-sustaining speed, unreachable by the starter alone: a hung start with fuel never lit.
failures.name: APU igniter failure

failures.cause: Fuel flow freezes at whatever it was delivering; over- or under-fuels the combustor from then on regardless of the governor's command.
failures.name: APU fuel control unit (metering valve) fault

failures.cause: A single channel's bias is masked by the other, still-valid channel's own vote/average (ecb.rs::Ecb::step) -- only when both channels are biased the same way, or both fail outright (its own separate 'dual channel speed loss' condition), does the governor see a wrong or missing speed and either overfuel toward overspeed or lose control entirely.
failures.name: APU ECB channel A/B speed pickup fault

failures.cause: Tank level falls; the pump progressively starves as level drops below the low-level threshold, pressure falls, and sustained low pressure while running trips low oil pressure protection.
failures.name: APU oil leak

failures.cause: Door fails to reach fully open, imposing a continuing inlet total-pressure loss that reduces available power and raises EGT for the same demand.
failures.name: APU inlet door actuator jam

failures.cause: More shaft power needed for the same electrical output, loading the core's torque balance.
failures.name: APU generator 1 winding/bearing wear

failures.cause: Removes the normal clamp at rated shaft power: an overloaded generator keeps demanding ever more shaft torque instead of being current-limited.
failures.name: APU generator 1 overload protection failure

failures.cause: More shaft power needed for the same electrical output, loading the core's torque balance.
failures.name: APU generator 2 winding/bearing wear

failures.cause: Removes the normal clamp at rated shaft power: an overloaded generator keeps demanding ever more shaft torque instead of being current-limited.
failures.name: APU generator 2 overload protection failure

failures.cause: Cockpit-indicated EGT reads low relative to the true turbine-exit temperature, masking a real overtemperature from the crew/ECAM; the true physics and the hard protective trip are unaffected.
failures.name: APU ECB channel A/B EGT thermocouple fault

failures.cause: A real fire is never confirmed: automatic fuel/bleed shutoff never commands and the bottle cannot be commanded to discharge.
failures.name: APU fire loop failure

failures.cause: Fire is confirmed and shutoff still commands, but the extinguisher bottle never discharges.
failures.name: APU fire bottle squib failure

failures.cause: FwdLowerCrewRest smoke concentration rises, sampled by deep::sensors' new FWD Lower Crew Rest detector (E-FIRE §B), which serves both the module's own smoke alert and the LOWER DECK LAVATORY alert (same module, same real lavatory); heat conducts into CargoFwd through the real structure link.

failures.cause: Heats that wing's leading-edge zone directly (real risk: an undetected WAI duct leak burning through the leading-edge structure, the well-publicised reason this class of system carries ODLS at all)

failures.cause: Mass flow escapes to the pylon zone (leak.rs::step); manifold/downstream pressure sags proportionally, and the pylon ODLS eventually trips on the resulting heat if severe enough
failures.name: Engine bleed duct leak

failures.cause: Large mass flow escapes as a near-sonic jet; above leak.rs::RUPTURE_JET_ONSET the jet is treated as impinging (higher heat-transfer effectiveness into the pylon zone), reliably tripping that pylon's ODLS and, once confirmed, latching that engine's isolation valve shut (network.rs)
failures.name: Engine bleed duct rupture

failures.cause: The pylon zone receives ordinary (non-fault) duct heat loss at up to 10x the healthy rate -- no ODLS trip on its own at normal bleed temperatures, but raises the pylon's baseline temperature so a subsequent leak trips ODLS sooner
failures.name: Engine bleed duct insulation damage

failures.cause: For the same cooling flow the outlet runs hotter (precooler.rs's NTU-effectiveness heat exchange); the FAV opens further to compensate, and at full fouling may not hold the outlet near target at all, raising overtemperature-trip risk
failures.name: Engine precooler fouling

failures.cause: No further cooling-flow modulation: stuck closed (or partly open) leaves the bleed hot regardless of demand; the hard overtemperature protection (true-temperature-based, module docs) is unaffected by this fault and can still force full flow via a separate path -- but a valve seized fully open cannot heed it either
failures.name: Engine precooler fan air valve stuck

failures.cause: The modulating FAV loop under/over-corrects against a stale reading; the independent hard overtemperature trip still sees the true temperature (precooler.rs module docs: a biased sensor cannot defeat it), so this fault degrades regulation quality without defeating the safety protection
failures.name: Engine precooler outlet temperature sensor fault

failures.cause: When duct pressure sags below ambient (e.g. low power, other faults), outside air is drawn back into the duct uncontrolled instead of being blocked, cooling/diluting it unpredictably
failures.name: Engine precooler check valve failure

failures.cause: Same as fault 1; heats the APU bay instead of a pylon
failures.name: APU bleed duct leak

failures.cause: Same as fault 2; can trip the APU bay ODLS and latch the APU isolation valve shut

failures.cause: Same as fault 3, applied to the APU bay zone
failures.name: APU bleed duct insulation damage

failures.cause: Same as fault 4
failures.name: APU precooler fouling

failures.cause: Same as fault 5
failures.name: APU precooler fan air valve stuck

failures.cause: Same as fault 6
failures.name: APU precooler outlet temperature sensor fault

failures.cause: Same as fault 7
failures.name: APU precooler check valve failure

failures.cause: Stuck shut: no HP6 backup once IP8 falls below the EASA switch-over pressure, engine duct pressure sags. Stuck open: continues drawing hot HP6 air even once IP8 alone would suffice, an avoidable EGT/performance penalty upstream at the compressor.
failures.name: Engine HP valve stuck

failures.cause: Stuck shut: that engine can no longer supply its own duct at all (a real 'ENG n BLEED FAULT'), leaving it dependent on cross-bleed. Stuck open: an ODLS trip's own isolation command can no longer close it, defeating the real isolation this system exists for.
failures.name: Engine PR (shutoff) valve stuck

failures.cause: The passive IP8 tap can no longer pass its normal share of flow, forcing the HP valve to open further/more often than normal to hold regulation -- a real, measurable shift from the efficient IP8 source to the costlier HP6 one.
failures.name: Engine IP8 check valve stuck closed

failures.cause: the masks still present -- that is the latch's job -- and that fraction of them delivers nothing when pulled; cabin oxygen flow and the generators' heat both fall in proportion, and the unfired generators are still full
failures.name: Passenger oxygen generator initiators dud

failures.cause: the burn stops early, so the cabin's oxygen stops before the rated 15 minutes are up and unburnt candle is left behind; at 0.5 the supply runs out after about seven and a half minutes
failures.name: Passenger oxygen candle quenches early

failures.cause: those units burn inside a closed PSU with no masks presented, reaching a case temperature near 300 C and putting their full chemical heat into the cabin zone until the candle is gone; the supply they represent is spent and cannot be recovered in flight
failures.name: Passenger oxygen generator inadvertent ignition

failures.cause: that fraction of the cabin gets no mask at all when the system deploys, so no generator in it is ever lit; the deployed fraction, the oxygen flow and the generator heat all fall together
failures.name: Passenger oxygen PSU latches seized

failures.cause: at full magnitude the cabin altitude trigger never presents the masks, however high the cabin goes; the flight deck's manual command is a separate path and still works, which is exactly why it is there
failures.name: Passenger oxygen automatic deployment controller failed

failures.cause: indicated first-aid bottle pressure falls steadily; once it drops below about half the 50 psi delivery setting the outlets stop flowing entirely, and the cabin has no therapeutic oxygen at all
failures.name: First-aid oxygen cylinder leak

failures.cause: past about a third the disc ruptures at the cylinder's own charge pressure and dumps it overboard in well under a minute
failures.name: First-aid oxygen overpressure disc degraded

failures.cause: delivery pressure falls; below half setting the continuous-flow outlets stop delivering, with the bottle still full
failures.name: First-aid oxygen regulator setting low

failures.cause: the cylinder bleeds down over hours into the low-pressure side with nobody using it, so the bottle is found short at the next check
failures.name: First-aid oxygen regulator seat leak

failures.cause: a continuous-flow outlet does not care whether anyone is breathing through it, so each stuck outlet drains the cylinder at its full 4 L/min and the supply is gone long before it is wanted
failures.name: First-aid oxygen outlet stuck open
